title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. The chosen elements keep their relative order but need not be adjacent.
constraints: 1 <= nums.Length <= 2500 on the examples, 100000 on the stress case
hints: The O(n^2) DP, where length[i] is the best subsequence ending at i, is the natural first solution. It will not survive the stress case.
For O(n log n), keep a list where tails[L] is the smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length L+1. That list is always sorted.
For each value, binary search for its insertion point: replace if it lands inside, append if it is larger than everything. The answer is the final list length.

cases.name: stress: 100k values (quadratic DP will not finish)
